entities.summary: John Stewart, 1st Earl of Atholl, also known as Sir John Stewart of Balveny, was a Scottish nobleman and ambassador who played a crucial role in the politics of medieval Scotland. Born around 1450, Stewart was a member of the powerful Stewart dynasty, which produced several Scottish monarchs. He was appointed as a regent for his nephew, James IV of Scotland, and later became a key advisor to the king. Stewart's diplomatic efforts helped to secure a peace treaty with France, which had long been a thorn in the side of Scottish rulers. He also played a role in the negotiations that led to the signing of the Treaty of Perpetual Peace between Scotland and England in 1502. Stewart's legacy as a diplomat and statesman has endured, with many historians praising his ability to navigate the complex web of alliances and rivalries that characterized medieval European politics. He died on September 15, 1512, at the age of around 62. Stewart's contributions to Scottish history are still felt today, and he remains one of the most fascinating figures of the medieval period.
